limits.what: A session that runs on Boat. The verify stack has no Boat. A box run that needs it starts its check VM with pnpm verify vm up --boat (four at once, one per Boat slot), which serves its own Tailscale Funnel; a Boat session in a project with resources (@db) still needs VM 131.

Upgrading or migrating an install that already holds people's data. A local stack starts with an empty database. A box run goes to a check VM on this machine (pnpm verify vm up), which holds the daily run's data.
The preview deploy itself: the script only runs on a server installed with mend server setup, a check VM (pnpm verify vm up) or the box.

An agent really running a turn. A local stack has no real agent login: its recipes sign agents in with published fake values the provider refuses, so no Claude or Codex turn runs there. A box run goes to a check VM on this machine (pnpm verify vm up), which holds the daily run's real logins (with --boat when it also needs Boat). A route of the new web app (apps/web) sent here runs from its checkout: pnpm verify drive new-web --box serves it in front of the check VM's or the box's API, so a change that is only apps/web and packages/ui needs no preview deploy (the verify skill, section 9).
